To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an approach for automatic building of multi-agent systems based on the concept of schemes, and we demonstrate the approach using simple examples.

1) the concept of schemes can be used for representation of connected groups in multi-agent systems; 2) evolutionary algorithm and a logic resolution system can be successfully combined for automatic building of new schemes to solve computational intelligence tasks.

we have proposed and implemented a new method for automatic construction of multi-agent schemes for solving computational intelligence tasks, based on evolutionary algorithms and a formal logic system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a problem of building a multi-agent system to solve a computational intelligence task.
the development of a formal framework for automatic composition of multiagent systems, which is a very important issue in the area of multiagent systems.
the problem of automatic composition (design) of multi-agent systems satisfying given constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a promising way of automatic building of computational agents’ schemes.
the proposed approach is a promising way to solve the problem of automatic composition.
the proposed methodology can be used for automatic generation of new schemes for a given computational intelligence problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolutionary search can be applied to the ontology-based search in order to build a new scheme of agents which is able to solve a given task.
we propose a new concept for representation and search of multi-agent system structures.
we have developed a method for automatic generation and evolution of schemes for computational agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach can help to build more complex schemes, which can be used in more complex multi-agent systems.
the combination of an evolutionary and an ontological approach can lead to a new class of algorithms which can automatically build and verify schemes.
the combination of evolutionary algorithms and logic resolution systems is able to automatically generate and test new schemes for multi-agent system composition.
